subject: dynamic number of independent variables for linear regression lm()

messages.author: 49a87a8d4d680c65
messages.subject: dynamic number of independent variables for linear regression lm()
parts:
I am using rHipe map reduce to perform linear regression in my mapper. It takes in a directory and runs regression on each file. However, each file has a different number of columns (ie. different number of x variables).

I know the way to call the linear regression function is lm(y~ x1 + x2 + x3... +xn), and I am able to generate dynamically N number of xn columns and assign them to the correct column in the file. My question is, how can I dynamically call the lm() function with my different xn variables?

ie.
 
lm (y~x1+x2+x3)
lm (y~x1+x2+x3+x4+x5)
lm (y~x1)
...

thanks so much in advance!

messages.author: 5b0c9158bfa781ba
messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] dynamic number of independent variables for linear regression lm()
parts:
This is not really a RHIPE question but here goes.
Is this all the columns? If so, y ~ .  will do the trick.

Do you want a subset of columns? Suppose the columns given by x1,x2,x3?
Then fml = as.formula(" y ~ x1+x2+x3")

then lm(fml, data=d) will do it.
